title: Positional chemical manufacture of macroscopic, atomically specified matter

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a way to manufacture a macroscopic three-dimensional object from a written atomic plan: specifying which atoms occupy which positions throughout its functional structure, then experimentally verifying that the manufactured object follows that plan. The central ambition is to extend positional control beyond selected surface sites or device layers to an object large enough to exhibit bulk function, including deliberately aperiodic arrangements that cannot be described by repeating a simple crystal unit cell. This is a proposed capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

The technical foundation described in the supplied April 2025 roadmap is narrower but substantial. Hydrogen depassivation lithography can expose individual reactive sites on silicon; silicon dangling-bond patterns and precisely incorporated dopants can define electronic structures whose behavior depends on atomic configuration. The roadmap also describes buried components and stacked semiconductor architectures. The proposed innovation would extend these forms of control to much broader chemically viable compositions and three-dimensional arrangements. It does not require that every imagined atomic plan be physically realizable.

significance.text: The roadmap already connects device and material properties to the number and positions of dopant atoms. Extending that principle throughout a functional bulk object would make internal atomic arrangement a much more extensive manufacturing variable. The revolutionary step would therefore be the breadth, depth and scale of positional control, rather than the first appearance of atomic precision in chemistry or materials fabrication.

Conditional synthesis: if achieved, this capability could let manufacturers prescribe local composition, interfaces and functional regions within one object, and deliberately construct arrangements inaccessible to an available statistical fabrication process. A convincing consequence would be a reproducible bulk function that depends on the specified arrangement, rather than composition alone. Such control could broaden the design space for materials and integrated devices, but would not guarantee superior performance, economical production or stability under operating conditions.

The manufacturing analogy has important limits. Ordinary chemistry already produces precisely structured molecules, and existing semiconductor processes already create buried and layered devices. The proposal should not be framed as replacing an entirely statistical world with the first atomically designed matter. Nor would one successful object establish universal assembly, arbitrary molecular synthesis at useful rates or mole-scale production. Those are additional capabilities with separate feasibility and scaling questions.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a demonstrated process that carries a specified atomic arrangement throughout a macroscopic three-dimensional object across a substantially broader chemical scope than the semiconductor platforms documented here. The roadmap's serial, two-dimensional dangling-bond printing and its successive patterning and epitaxial-growth approaches provide different partial foundations. Stacking aligned device layers is meaningful three-dimensional fabrication, but does not by itself establish independent specification of atomic identities and positions throughout an arbitrary bulk structure.

For the documented silicon platform, the roadmap identifies printing speed, error-free fabrication, encapsulation and further device development as remaining challenges. Its discussion of extending precise growth to metals, additional semiconductors and dielectrics is conditional, including the need for precision in both lateral and vertical dimensions while preserving chemical purity. These requirements show why success with one surface chemistry cannot simply be assumed to transfer to many materials.

Engineering synthesis: broader positional manufacture would need compatible ways to deliver and react building species at intended sites, preserve previously constructed regions during later steps, reach or construct interior sites, and detect and correct defects as the object grows. It would also need to reconcile throughput with precision and verify buried structure at meaningful coverage. A written arrangement must remain chemically and mechanically viable during fabrication and use. These are concrete requirements inferred from the proposed capability; the supplied evidence does not establish a general solution or determine whether mole-scale manufacture is feasible.

current_state.text: The supplied research dates the Schofield et al. Nano Futures roadmap, volume 9, article 012001, to 15 April 2025. In section 3.4, Robert A. Wolkow, Lucian Livadaru and Jason Pitters describe the central manufacturing challenges as essentially resolved specifically for silicon dangling bonds. The supplied review reports error-free ensembles containing more than 100 dangling bonds. This is evidence of atomic precision within that platform, not a demonstration of macroscopic three-dimensional matter with broadly selectable chemistry.

The same section treats printing billions of atoms in 10 hours as an aspirational throughput target. Its expectation of error-free printing of many thousands of atoms is a forecast, not a reported completed demonstration. Dangling-bond printing is described as serial and as producing two-dimensional circuitry, with components completed in one pass. The section authors' optimism must therefore be read alongside the remaining speed and device-development requirements.

The roadmap's broader coverage includes atomically engineered dopant devices, buried structures and three-dimensional semiconductor architectures made by successive patterning and epitaxial growth. It reports that multiple device layers can be stacked and aligned with nanometre precision within the same silicon crystal. That alignment precision should not be confused with arbitrary atom-by-atom specification between and throughout the layers. These results correct the earlier blanket description of the field as producing only surface electronic elements.

This account relies on the supplied review of an identity-verified alternative PDF, rather than a new inspection of the article. The retained extraction was partial and ended during section 4.4; section 3.4 and the passages supporting the distinctions above were available to the reviewer. The record contains no later research coverage establishing progress through 1 November 2026. It also does not establish a field-wide absence of arbitrary atomic specification in a biological-cell-sized object. These limits leave that absence claim unresolved; they do not show that the reported semiconductor results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: manufacture a three-dimensional object with a specified aperiodic atomic structure, large enough to handle and evaluate as a bulk functional object, and show experimentally that its structure follows the advance specification. Before fabrication, define the object's dimensions, intended composition, positional tolerances, allowed defects and verification coverage. These are proposed benchmark elements, not an established community standard; 'large enough to handle' still requires an operational definition.
completion_criteria.label: Manufactured three-dimensional bulk aperiodic structure experimentally matches atomic specification

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification: use complementary structural and compositional measurements that address interior regions as well as accessible surfaces, and report uncertainty, detection limits and unexamined regions. Distinguish directly measured agreement from agreement inferred through a validated manufacturing process. If verification covers only a sample of sites, report the resulting confidence and coverage rather than claiming that every atom has been checked.
completion_criteria.label: Structural and compositional verification reports interior coverage and measurement limits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional test: demonstrate a useful behavior attributable to the specified arrangement, with controls of the same composition produced through a relevant statistical process and, where feasible, controls with deliberately altered arrangements. The comparison should support a defined arrangement-dependent advantage under stated conditions. It cannot establish that every possible statistical material of that composition would lack the behavior.
completion_criteria.label: Specified arrangement demonstrates useful advantage over same-composition statistical controls

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: repeat fabrication across independently produced objects and seek independent reproduction, reporting yield, defect distribution, throughput, stability and operating conditions. Demonstrating different structures and compositions would establish increasing breadth, not literal universality. Wafer-scale dangling-bond circuits alone would leave the bulk three-dimensional target open; a successful narrow bulk demonstration would still leave wider chemical scope, cost and mole-scale production unresolved.
completion_criteria.label: Repeated fabrication across independent objects reports performance and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-04, Practical, on-demand synthesis of arbitrary stable molecules, shares the ambition of broad chemical construction. Producing a collection of identical specified molecules primarily addresses that molecular-synthesis goal. CHEMREV-10 instead centers on spatial specification throughout a macroscopic three-dimensional object, potentially with an aperiodic internal arrangement. One manufacturing platform could contribute to both entries, but useful-rate molecular synthesis and bulk positional manufacture are distinct demonstrations. Only CHEMREV-04's roster title was supplied, so this boundary remains provisional.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-09, Phase-pure synthesis of arbitrary designed crystalline solids, overlaps in making designed solid matter. Its stated target concerns obtaining a desired crystalline phase; CHEMREV-10 concerns prescribed atomic placement throughout an object, including nonrepeating structures and intentionally different local regions. A phase-pure crystal could be relevant evidence without satisfying this entry's aperiodic bulk demonstration, while an atomically specified heterogeneous object need not be a single crystalline phase. This comparison is based on the supplied title, not a full CHEMREV-09 record.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-01, A method that predicts realistic chemical outcomes before the experiment, and CHEMREV-05, Enzyme-level catalysts on request for arbitrary reactions, could provide enabling capabilities for choosing feasible construction steps. Prediction and catalysis would not themselves establish positional manufacture. CHEMREV-03's ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductor is a possible application target only if a suitable structure exists and can be fabricated; positional control alone would not establish superconductivity. These are conditional relationships inferred from the roster, not demonstrated dependencies.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish developments after April 2025 or the field's status on 1 November 2026.
The reviewed extraction ends during section 4.4, limiting conclusions about material outside the retained text.
Whether any method has achieved arbitrary atomic specification throughout a biological-cell-sized object remains unresolved by the supplied evidence.
The feasible chemical scope, defect tolerance, throughput, economics and prospects for mole-scale manufacture remain undetermined.
The proposed benchmark still needs numerical definitions of macroscopic size, positional tolerances, acceptable defects, verification confidence and functional advantage.
The supplied roster permits provisional comparisons with CHEMREV-04 and CHEMREV-09, but their full records are needed to confirm the boundaries.

brief.title: Objects built to an atom-by-atom plan
possible: Manufacturers could build an object whose internal structure follows a written plan for which atoms go where. The control would extend throughout an object large enough to handle and test, including arrangements that do not simply repeat a crystal pattern.

A single object could contain precisely designed regions with different compositions and functions, joined at planned boundaries. Measurements would establish how closely its interior follows the design.
why: For material and device designers, the arrangement of atoms throughout an object would become a manufacturing choice. They could pursue useful behavior that depends on where atoms sit, beyond what the same ingredients alone provide.

sources.showed: Their roadmap describes electronic devices built with precisely placed atoms, buried components and stacked device layers within silicon.
sources.cited_for: Atomic placement already controls electronic structures, providing a foundation for broader manufacture.
sources.not_established: These semiconductor results do not establish control of atomic identities and positions throughout a bulk object across broader chemistry.

sources.who: Megan Cowie and colleagues at CBN Nano Technologies
sources.showed: The team used positioned molecules to transfer carbon pairs onto selected silicon sites and extend carbon chains by forming further bonds.
sources.quote:
We
demonstrate single-site C2 donation, spatially patterned multi-site C 2 donation, and the stepwise
assembly of polyyne structures through successive C-C bond formation.
sources.cited_for: Repeated placement and bond formation provide a step toward building structures to an atomic plan.
sources.not_established: Small carbon structures attached to silicon do not establish a bulk object with a specified interior or useful bulk function.

shown: The silicon work summarized by Schofield and colleagues includes error-free patterns of more than 100 dangling bonds: reactive sites where silicon atoms have an unpaired electron. Researchers have also stacked device layers, extending fabrication beneath the surface.

In a preprint, Cowie and colleagues report an 18-atom carbon pattern and stepwise chain growth on silicon. This adds controlled chemical construction to site placement, but remains a small structure attached to a surface.
missing: A process still needs to build a specified atomic arrangement throughout a handleable object across substantially broader chemistry.
Construction needs to preserve earlier regions, build the interior and control defects while maintaining useful speed.
Measurements need to establish agreement with the atomic plan inside the object, with meaningful coverage.
Repeated objects need to show useful behavior caused by their planned arrangement.

milestones.label: A bulk object matches its atomic plan
milestones.explanation: A handleable object with a nonrepeating atomic arrangement would have to match a plan with predefined size, tolerances and allowed defects. This would extend positional control throughout a functional object.

milestones.label: Interior measurements establish how much of the plan matches
milestones.explanation: Complementary measurements would have to report interior composition and structure, coverage and uncertainty, separating observation from inference. This would establish how much of the claimed agreement is supported.

milestones.label: The planned arrangement provides a useful advantage
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to show an arrangement-dependent advantage over objects of the same composition made by a relevant statistical process. This would connect atomic placement to useful function.

milestones.label: Repeated manufacture establishes reliability and practical limits
milestones.explanation: Repeated fabrication would have to report yield, defects, speed and stability, with independent reproduction sought. This would establish reliability and practical boundaries; broader chemistry would require further demonstrations.

uncertain: The range of workable compositions, tolerable defects and stable atomic arrangements remains unknown.
Useful production speed, cost and the feasibility of making large quantities remain open.
The benchmark still needs numerical thresholds for object size, placement accuracy, measurement confidence and functional advantage.

page.title: Macroscopic atomically precise manufacturing
page.definition: Positionally controlled chemical reactions manufacture macroscopic three-dimensional products with specified atomic identities and relative positions throughout their functional structure. Designs include aperiodic regions, whose atomic arrangement does not repeat a unit cell.

goal.need: The roadmap published on 15 April 2025 reports error-free ensembles of more than 100 silicon dangling bonds, sites with unpaired electrons. It also estimates more than 200 hours to write 1 µm² at 0.768 nm resolution with a serial tool. DOE’s September 2019 comparison below shows why dopant placement requires control at atomic spacings. The manufacturing goal extends this control to the interior of bulk products.

figures.caption: Placement scales in DOE’s September 2019 project brief
figures.note: These are historical project figures. Resolution, atomic spacing and target accuracy are different quantities.

statements.body: U.S. Department of Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office
statements.quote: automated, programmable, atomically precise manufacturing using positional assembly
statements.context: AMO Multi-Year Program Plan Target 5.4.3, reproduced in the project’s programme-review presentation.

statements.quote: low-cost atomically precise manufacturing of macroscopic products.
statements.context: The workshop whitepaper identifies this as the longer-term objective of a proposed atomic-precision research initiative.

statements.quote: If we can specify a structure, we set out to build exactly that structure — and verify it.
statements.context: The developer’s statement of its manufacturing objective; the page is undated and carries a 2026 copyright.

completion.title: A macroscopic three-dimensional product is manufactured and verified against its atomic design.
completion.criterion: Manufacture a macroscopic three-dimensional product with a predeclared atomic design that includes aperiodic regions. Establish experimental agreement of atomic identities, relative structural sites and bonding throughout its functional volume, including buried interfaces. Apply DOE’s atomically precise definition: no defects, missing atoms, extra atoms or incorrect atoms. No external numerical boundary for macroscopic size or verification coverage and confidence was located; those acceptance parameters remain unresolved.
completion.set_by: Atlas provisional qualitative test, combining the published macroscopic-manufacturing objective with DOE’s definition of atomic precision.
completion.basis: Searched DOE AMO definitions and project targets, DARPA A2P, Foresight Feynman Grand Prize rules, and the 2007 and 2025 roadmaps for a whole-volume macroscopic acceptance test; none was located. The 2007 roadmap explicitly avoids sharp scale, complexity and defect thresholds. Its projected capability levels therefore do not constitute acceptance criteria. The provisional test retains the stated capability while leaving the missing quantitative boundaries explicit.

milestones.title: A fabricated electronic device resolves the effect of individual dopant atoms.
milestones.criterion: Fabricate and electrically test a device sensitive to individual dopant atoms, meeting the project’s Budget Period 1 go/no-go goal. The programme-review presentation for 11–12 June 2019 reports this goal as 100% complete. That percentage denotes milestone completion, not device yield; the slide does not specify the number of tested devices. This is a programme report, not a peer-reviewed result.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Department of Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office; Budget Period 1 go/no-go goal for Atomically Precise Manufacturing for 2D-Designed Materials, reported by Zyvex Labs.
milestones.threshold_quote: Demonstrated device with sensitivity to single atoms

milestones.title: Atomically designed silicon materials containing two dopant species are fabricated and tested.
milestones.criterion: Fabricate and test two-dimensional designer materials containing two different dopant species, and establish design rules for each dopant. The project specifies placement within a plane of silicon. The 2025 roadmap reports a defect-free 2 × 2 array of four individual arsenic dopants; that single-species result alone does not establish this two-species endpoint.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Department of Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office; published project milestones for Automated Manufacturing of 2D Atomically Precise and Robust Devices in Silicon Substrates. This endpoint was written for doped silicon.
milestones.threshold_quote: Fabricate and test 2D designer materials made with two different species

milestones.title: Mechanosynthesis reshapes a scanning-probe tip into a predefined three-dimensional crystalline form.
milestones.criterion: Use a surface-anchored molecular tool and externally controlled three-dimensional movement to remove selected atoms from a scanning-probe microscope tip until it has a predefined crystalline form. This is mechanosynthesis: chemical reactions controlled by mechanical positioning. Related evidence: Cowie and colleagues’ preprint submitted on 26 May 2026 reports four C₂ transfers producing an eight-carbon surface pattern and successive carbon–carbon bond formation. It does not establish the sculpted-tip endpoint and is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Department of Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office; project objective in A Radical Tool for 3D Atomically Precise Sculpting. The objective concerns a scanning-probe tip.
milestones.threshold_quote: produce an atomically precise SPM tip by sequentially removing defect atoms

milestones.title: An integrated process assembles a macroscopic 3D workpiece from atomically specified parts.
milestones.criterion: A programmable process manufactures atomically specified three-dimensional parts and joins them into a macroscopic workpiece, preserving the parts’ structures and the designed atomic registry and bonding at their interfaces. This adopts the 2025 roadmap’s hierarchical assembly route as a provisional integration test. Complete verification throughout the workpiece’s functional volume is reserved for completion. No external workpiece-size or interface-acceptance threshold was located.
milestones.set_by: Atlas provisional integration test. Searches of DOE project targets and the 2007 and 2025 roadmaps located a hierarchical-assembly objective, but no published acceptance test for this integrated result.

not_found: No published acceptance test for whole-volume macroscopic positional manufacture was located in DOE and DARPA programmes, Foresight prize rules, or the 2007 and 2025 roadmaps.
No common numerical boundary for macroscopic size or required interior verification coverage and confidence was found.
A result establishing DOE’s two-species designer-material endpoint was not located.
A final experimental demonstration of DOE’s predefined three-dimensional sculpted-tip endpoint was not located.

results.finding: Mechanosynthetic formation of the final eight-carbon surface pattern succeeded in 27 of 32 attempts (84%).
results.detail: The final-step yield is conditional on the required precursor. The work demonstrates controlled carbon transfer and bond formation on the probe chip, but does not sculpt its tip into a predefined three-dimensional crystalline form.

results.finding: The BP1 single-atom-sensitive device milestone was reported 100% complete; the number of tested devices was not specified.
results.detail: The percentage reports milestone completion, not device yield. This is a programme-review presentation.
results.quote:
BP1 Go/No Go goal: Demonstrated device with 
sensitivity to single atoms: 100%

results.finding: One transistor attributed to a single phosphorus dopant showed a 60 meV electron addition energy.
results.detail: The authors report electrical measurements consistent with a single dopant, but say the transport data cannot fully exclude multiple dopants. The paper does not report the Budget Period 1 go/no-go goal or its completion.
results.quote:
The D − state is where the chemical potential has been lowered an additional
60 meV (the so-called addition energy) and a second electron
has been added to the atom.

results.finding: A single-atom transistor: one device with one phosphorus dopant atom.
results.detail: Millikelvin electron transport measurements resolved discrete quantum levels. The source does not establish that the device met the specified programme goal or that the goal was reported 100% complete.
results.quote: The transistor operates at liquid helium temperatures, and millikelvin electron transport measurements confirm the presence of discrete quantum levels in the energy spectrum of the phosphorus atom.

results.finding: One silicon bipolar p–n junction combining boron and phosphorus doping was fabricated and electrically tested; it was 100 nm wide.
results.detail: The result demonstrates a device using two dopant species, but the supplied text does not establish atomically specified placement or design rules for each dopant.
results.quote: By combining our p-type doping approach with established phosphine-based n-type doping, we fabricate a 100-nm-wide p–n junction and show that its electrical behaviour is similar to that of an Esaki diode.

results.finding: Surface-anchored molecular tools abstracted silicon in 163 of 163 interactions on scanning-probe chips.
results.detail: The experiments used lateral targeting and z-axis motion at 4 K and 77 K. They produced vacancies and subtractive surface patterns, but did not establish a predefined three-dimensional crystalline tip form.
results.quote:
Instead, abstraction was the only outcome when following z-only, on-dimer trajectories 
with MAOC–C 2I, both at 4 K (63/63 interactions) and 77 K (100/100 interactions), further 
supporting the interpretation of the SiV feature as silicon abstraction.
